instruction.what: The evidence validation (B5) of one subgroup, after its sweep, the gate before 3.1: the code checks of its observations (shown in `code_checks`), and the reading of every evidence observation of the subgroup (its own of S1 to 2.1, and the older ones on its occurrences kept as evidence) for whether it is true, founded and coherent with the others. Inner being is not judged here; the two validations are never run together.
read: Read the code checks first: a failing check names observations to repair (unmarked, no node, a word node missing a column without its reason, a trace to a deleted observation, two of one text, a B1 observation no sense traces, a sense the 2.1 observations on its occurrences do not trace, an older observation left open).

Take one observation at a time (`observations`, in the order of the steps): its text, basis and grounds against its verses (`verses`) and the observations it traces. Is it true of those verses? Does it say more than they show? Does it contradict another observation of the subgroup?
write: Fill `answer.observations`, one entry for each observation of the package: verdict true, with `why` (what in the verses and the data bears it out); or verdict repair, with `why` (what is wrong) and `actions`: the actions of the validation that repair it (cfg_setting validate.reading actions, each with its parameters, for example {"action": "restate", "oid": id, "new_text": ..., "checked": ..., "reason": ...}, or delete_neither, complete_node, add_trace).
A repair is checked as it is written; an observation that cannot be made true is deleted with its reason.

Then: Collection-Build.ps1 -Action RecordEvidence -File <the answer file> (-Check to preview), and ReadEvidence again until every evidence observation is read; the gate passes when all are read and the code checks pass.

keep.text: A sheet of validation actions is checked whole (every action named, its parameters complete) and written in one transaction: any action the tables refuse refuses the whole sheet and nothing is kept. -Check runs every action and rolls back. Every change is kept in ib_observation_change with its reason (RW-01); nothing is physically deleted.

A finding of the validation is repaired first: a wording that is untrue or stronger than its verse is restated and the restatement checked against the base data; a node missing a column is completed, or the reason the data cannot give it is recorded; a duplicate is consolidated; a node is deleted only when another live node carries its occurrence or it supports no finding of its observation. A finding is left open only when a named collection's validation will touch the observation: the deferral to that collection and the finding are recorded, and the check accepts it as deferred. A finding with no named owner is closed in the validation.

An older observation is deleted as consumed only when live observations carry its meaning: every word occurrence of it is on a live node of a carrier or named as not carried with its reason, the mapping is stated in words (what the old says, which carrier states each part), the traces to it are re-pointed or replaced, and the consumption is kept as `consumed_by`. An observation that holds more than one finding is split first.

An observation that is neither evidence nor inner being contributes nothing to the purposes of the observations (researcher, 2026-11-22): it is commented with its reason and the word occurrences no other live observation holds, then deleted. An observation already marked, or one another observation traces, is not deleted this way.

Evidence states what the data are or show, tied to a verse. Inner being states how something works in the inner being, based on evidence, a building block of the stage 5 claims. The marker (ib_observation.nature) follows the content and purpose of the observation, never its stage (RS-04): an observation of any stage may be inner being when it traces to evidence. One that states both is split. The marker is set when the observation is created, by the item that is answered (cfg_setting layer.reading items.<item>.nature); a finding file never sets it; the validation changes it only where the content shows the item's nature does not hold.

The validation runs in two layers, never concurrently: evidence first, then inner being. The inner-being layer is judged only when the evidence layer passes (every in-scope observation marked, none without a live node, no word node missing a required column without its reason, no live trace to a deleted observation, no two of one meaning). A later evidence change reopens only the inner-being rows it touches. In the build this gate is: step 3.1 does not open before the evidence layer passes, and step 3.3 does not close before both layers pass (cfg_setting layer.reading open_gate and closing_gate).
No observation is changed except by a reading, and every change is recorded with its reason. An observation no longer supported by the verse is soft-deleted, with the reason.
One observation per finding: the same description is never written twice. Applied to another verse, word or scope it gains a node on the existing observation.
Observation text is concise and tied to this verse's content, never a restatement of the word's dictionary sense. A transliteration is never given without its gloss.
Verse references are resolved fresh at write time, never taken from the text written. Relations are recorded only on evidence.
Missing data in the base extract is named as a gap, never substituted from memory or outside knowledge.

observations.text: God is named as the one before whom, or toward whom, the meditation is set: before God in Job 15:4, acceptable in the sight of the Lord in Psa 19:14, pleasing to him in Psa 104:34, the law of the Lord in Psa 1:2, and God remembered in Psa 77:3.
observations.grounds: hindering meditation before God

observations.text: In Pro 5:21 the Lord is named as the one who ponders: he weighs the paths of a man, whose ways are before his eyes.
observations.grounds: he ponders all his paths

observations.text: People are named as the ones who meditate or ponder: Isaac in Gen 24:63, your servant in Psa 119:23, and in Act 10:19 the one pondering the vision, with the men who come to him named after it.
observations.grounds: Isaac went out to meditate

observations.text: In 1Ki 18:27 the musing is said of a god, in Elijah's mockery: Elijah is named as the speaker, and the god of the others is the one who may be musing.
observations.grounds: Either he is musing

observations.text: In Psa 19:14 and Psa 104:34 the meditation runs from the person to God as something offered: it is to be acceptable in his sight, pleasing to him.
observations.grounds: May my meditation be pleasing to him

observations.text: In Psa 1:2, Psa 77:3 and Job 15:4 the meditation runs from the person toward what is God's: his law, God remembered, meditation before God.
observations.grounds: on his law he meditates

observations.text: In Pro 5:21 the pondering runs from God to man: the Lord weighs the paths of a man.
observations.grounds: he ponders all his paths

observations.text: In Gen 24:63, Psa 119:23 and Act 10:19 the meditating or pondering is the person's own and turned inward: Isaac in the field with no object named, the servant on the statutes, and in Act 10:19 a word comes to the one pondering while he ponders.
observations.grounds: while Peter was pondering the vision

observations.text: In 1Ki 18:27 the word runs from Elijah to the prophets, in mockery: the musing he names is a state he ascribes to their god.
observations.grounds: Elijah mocked them

observations.text: In Psa 145:5 wondrous (H6381) stands two words before meditate and describes what is meditated on: the works of God are the object, set first in the verse.
observations.grounds: on your wondrous works, I will meditate

observations.text: In Jos 1:8 careful (H8104J) stands four words after meditate, in the purpose it serves: the meditating day and night is so that the person keeps to doing what is written.
observations.grounds: so that you may be careful to do

observations.text: In Psa 119:99 more understanding (H7919A) opens the verse and the meditation closes it as its ground: the testimonies being the speaker's meditation is given as why he understands more than his teachers.
observations.grounds: for your testimonies are my meditation

observations.text: In Psa 1:2 delight (H2656) opens the verse and the meditating follows in the next clause, both on the law of the Lord: the delight and the meditation have one object.
observations.grounds: his delight is in the law of the Lord

observations.text: In Psa 104:34 pleasing (H6149) stands directly after meditation and says what the speaker asks of it: that it please the Lord.
observations.grounds: May my meditation be pleasing to him

observations.text: In Jos 1:8 depart (H4185) stands three words before meditate, in the clause it is set against: the book is not to leave the mouth, and instead it is meditated on.
observations.grounds: shall not depart from your mouth

observations.text: In Psa 38:12 ruin (H1942) stands directly before meditate, the speaking of ruin joined to the devising of treachery by those who seek harm.
observations.grounds: speak of ruin and meditate treachery

observations.text: In Psa 119:78 wronged (H5791) stands three words before meditate, in the clause about the insolent; the speaker's meditating is set against their wronging.
observations.grounds: they have wronged me with falsehood

observations.text: In Pro 15:28 wicked (H7563) stands three words after ponders, on the other side of the contrast: the righteous heart ponders, the mouth of the wicked pours out.
observations.grounds: the mouth of the wicked pours out evil things

observations.text: In Psa 77:3 faints (H5848C) stands two words after meditate, in the same clause: when the speaker meditates, his spirit faints.
observations.grounds: when I meditate, my spirit faints

observations.text: In Job 15:4 fear (H3374) stands two words before meditation, in the first of two parallel charges: the fear of God is set aside, and meditation before God is held back.
observations.grounds: doing away with the fear of God

observations.text: In Psa 63:6, Psa 77:3, Psa 77:6 and Psa 143:5 remember (H2142) stands before meditate, one to three words ahead, in parallel clauses: remembering comes first and meditating follows.
observations.grounds: I remember the days of old; I meditate

observations.text: In Psa 104:34 rejoice (H8055) stands three words after meditation, in the clause that follows it: the speaker rejoices in the Lord.
observations.grounds: for I rejoice in the Lord

observations.text: In Psa 119:15, Psa 119:27 and Psa 119:78 precepts (H6490) stands beside meditate as what is meditated on, or as the way the speaker asks to understand before he meditates.
observations.grounds: I will meditate on your precepts

observations.text: In Psa 19:14, Psa 49:3, Psa 77:6, Pro 15:28 and Luk 2:19 heart (H3820A, H3824, G2588) stands beside the meditation or the pondering, one to three words off, as where it takes place: the meditation of the heart, meditating in the heart, the heart that ponders.
observations.grounds: the meditation of my heart

observations.text: In Psa 77:12, Psa 143:5 and Psa 145:5 work and works (H6467, H4639G, H1697K) stand beside meditate as what is meditated on: the deeds of God.
observations.grounds: meditate on your mighty deeds

observations.text: In Psa 77:3 moan (H1993) stands one word before meditate, in the parallel clause: remembering God brings moaning, meditating brings the spirit's fainting.
observations.grounds: When I remember God, I moan

observations.text: In 1Ki 18:27 cry (H7121I) stands five words before musing, in Elijah's taunt: they are to cry out because their god may be musing and not hearing.
observations.grounds: Cry aloud, for he is a god

observations.text: In Psa 119:48 and Psa 119:97 love (H0157G) stands before the meditation, one to three words ahead, with one object: the commandments or the law that is loved is what is meditated on.
observations.grounds: Oh how I love your law! It is my meditation

observations.text: In Psa 145:5 glorious, splendor and majesty (H3519, H1926, H1935) open the verse, three to five words before meditate, and name the first object of the meditation: the splendor of God's majesty.
observations.grounds: On the glorious splendor of your majesty

observations.text: In Psa 77:12 mighty deeds (H5949) stands directly after meditate as its object: the deeds of God are what the speaker meditates on.
observations.grounds: meditate on your mighty deeds

observations.text: In Psa 38:12 hurt (H7451C) stands three words before meditate, naming what the ones who meditate treachery seek: the speaker's harm.
observations.grounds: those who seek my hurt

observations.text: In Psa 119:23 plotting (H1696G) stands two words before meditate, in the clause set against it: princes speak against the speaker, and he meditates on the statutes.
observations.grounds: princes sit plotting against me

observations.text: In Pro 15:28 answer (H6030B) stands directly after ponders as its object: the righteous heart ponders how to answer.
observations.grounds: ponders how to answer

observations.text: In Psa 119:148 promise (H0565A) stands two words after meditate as its object, and the waking eyes before the night watches are for this meditation.
observations.grounds: that I may meditate on your promise

observations.text: In Psa 119:78 falsehood (H8267) stands two words before meditate, naming how the insolent wronged the speaker; his meditating is set against it.
observations.grounds: wronged me with falsehood

observations.text: In Psa 143:5 old (H6924H) stands directly before meditate, in the clause before it: the days of old are what is remembered, and the meditating on God's deeds follows.
observations.grounds: I remember the days of old

observations.text: In Psa 19:14 acceptable (H7522) stands three words after meditation and says what the speaker asks for the meditation of his heart, with the words of his mouth: that they be accepted.
observations.grounds: be acceptable in your sight

observations.text: In Jos 1:8 prosperous (H6743B) stands ten words after meditate, in the outcome of the doing the meditation serves: the way made prosperous.
observations.grounds: make your way prosperous

observations.text: In Pro 15:28 righteous (H6662) stands directly before ponders and names whose heart ponders.
observations.grounds: The heart of the righteous ponders

observations.text: In 1Ki 18:27 aloud (H1419A, with H6963A at the same place) stands four words before musing and qualifies the crying Elijah calls for, not the musing.
observations.grounds: Cry aloud, for he is a god

verses.text: Those who seek my life lay their snares; those who seek my hurt speak of ruin and meditate treachery all day long.
My mouth shall speak wisdom; the meditation of my heart shall be understanding.
Even though princes sit plotting against me, your servant will meditate on your statutes.
But you are doing away with the fear of God and hindering meditation before God.
And while Peter was pondering the vision, the Spirit said to him, “ Behold, three men are looking for you.
And at noon Elijah mocked them, saying, “ Cry aloud, for he is a god. Either he is musing, or he is relieving himself, or he is on a journey, or perhaps he is asleep and must be awakened.”
The heart of the righteous ponders how to answer, but the mouth of the wicked pours out evil things.
When I remember God, I moan; when I meditate, my spirit faints. Selah
I said, “Let me remember my song in the night; let me meditate in my heart.” Then my spirit made a diligent search:
Let the insolent be put to shame, because they have wronged me with falsehood; as for me, I will meditate on your precepts.
but his delight is in the law of the Lord, and on his law he meditates day and night.
Let the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable in your sight, O Lord, my rock and my redeemer.
May my meditation be pleasing to him, for I rejoice in the Lord.
I will lift up my hands toward your commandments, which I love, and I will meditate on your statutes.
Mem Oh how I love your law! It is my meditation all the day.
On the glorious splendor of your majesty, and on your wondrous works, I will meditate.
Make me understand the way of your precepts, and I will meditate on your wondrous works.
And Isaac went out to meditate in the field toward evening. And he lifted up his eyes and saw, and behold, there were camels coming.
I will ponder all your work, and meditate on your mighty deeds.
I will meditate on your precepts and fix my eyes on your ways.
My eyes are awake before the watches of the night, that I may meditate on your promise.
I remember the days of old; I meditate on all that you have done; I ponder the work of your hands.
For a man’s ways are before the eyes of the Lord, and he ponders all his paths.

This Book of the Law shall not depart from your mouth, but you shall meditate on it day and night, so that you may be careful to do according to all that is written in it. For then you will make your way prosperous, and then you will have good success.
when I remember you upon my bed, and meditate on you in the watches of the night;
I have more understanding than all my teachers, for your testimonies are my meditation.
But Mary treasured up all these things, pondering them in her heart.
